Gray * ''[[Tema]]'' Adans. * ''[[Ornithospermum]]'' Durande, not validly published }} '''''Echinochloa''''' is a very widespread [[genus]] of plants in the [[Poaceae|grass family]] and tribe [[Paniceae]].[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/394132#page/137/mode/1up Palisot de Beauvois, Ambroise Marie François Joseph. 1812. Essai d'une Nouvelle Agrostographie 53] in Latin[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=111218 Flora of China Vol. 22 Page 515 稗属 bai shu ''Echinochloa'' P. Beauvois, Ess. Agrostogr. 53. 1812. ][http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=5&taxon_id=111218 Flora of Pakistan] Some of the species are known by the common names barnyard grass or cockspur grass.[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=echinochloa Altervista Flora Italiana, genere ''Echinochloa''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201022126/http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Echinochloa |date=2015-02-01 }}[http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=ECHIN4 US Department of Agriculture plants profile, ''Echinochloa'' P. Beauv., cockspur grass ] Some of the species within this genus are [[millet]]s that are grown as [[cereal]] or [[fodder]] crops. The most notable of these are [[Echinochloa esculenta|Japanese millet]] (''E. esculenta'') in [[East Asia]], [[Echinochloa frumentacea|Indian barnyard millet]] (''E. frumentacea'') in [[South Asia]], [[Echinochloa stagnina|burgu millet]] (''E. stagnina'') in [[West Africa]], and channel millet (''E. turneriana'') in arid and semi-arid inland Australia.{{Cite journal |last=Chandora |first=Rahul |last2=Furtado |first2=Agnelo |last3=Constantin |first3=Lena |last4=Silcock |first4=Jennifer |last5=Westaway |first5=Michael C. |last6=Henry |first6=Robert J. |date=2026-05-30 |title=Genome analysis of Channel millet reveals a wild dodecaploid shaped by environmental variability |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-73794-7 |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=7038 |doi=10.1038/s41467-026-73794-7 |doi-access=free|issn=2041-1723 |pmc=13392040 |pmid=42225664}}{{Citation |last=Kerkhove |first=Ray C. |title=Fish Traps, Seed-Grinding and Food Stores |date=2024-05-22 |work=The Oxford Handbook of Global Indigenous Archaeologies |url=https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordhb/9780197607695.013.60 |access-date=2026-08-28 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-760769-5 |last2=Silcock |first2=Jennifer L. |last3=Williams |first3=Douglas |last4=Kotarba-Morley |first4=Ania M. |last5=Keenan-Jones |first5=Duncan |last6=Wright |first6=Nathan J. |last7=Morley |first7=Mike W. |last8=Gorringe |first8=Joshua |last9=Scholz |first9=Glen}} Collectively, the members of this genus are called barnyard grasses (though this may also refer to ''[[Echinochloa crus-galli|E. crus-galli]]'' specifically), and are also known as barnyard millets or '''billion-dollar grasses'''. When not grown on purpose, these grasses may become a nuisance to farmers. In particular, [[echinochloa crus-galli|common barnyard grass]] (''E. crus-galli'') is notorious as a weed.{{aut|Pheng, S.; Khiev, B.; Pol, C. & Jahn, G.C.}} (2001): Response of two rice cultivars to the competition of ''Echinochloa crus-galli''. International Rice Research Institute Notes '''26'''(2): 36-37. [http://www.irri.org/publications/irrn/pdfs/vol26no2/irrn262pestsci.pdf PDF fulltext] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100705073019/http://www.irri.org/publications/irrn/pdfs/vol26no2/irrn262pestsci.pdf |date=2010-07-05 }} It is not easily suppressed with [[living mulch]]es such as [[mucuna pruriens|velvet bean]] (''Mucuna pruriens'' var. ''utilis'').{{aut|Caamal-Maldonado, J.A.; Jimenez, J.J.; Torres, A. & Anaya, A.}} (2001): The use of allelopathic legume cover and mulch species for weed control in cropping systems. Agronomy Journal '''93'''(1): 27-36. [http://agron.scijournals.org/cgi/reprint/93/1/27.pdf PDF fulltext]{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} [[echinochloa oryzoides|Early barnyard grass]] (''E. oryzoides'') is a well-known example of [[Vavilovian mimicry]]: the plants have [[evolution|evolved]] to resemble [[rice]] (''Oryza''), enabling them to escape [[weed control|weeding]] more easily.{{aut|Barrett, S.}} (1983): Mimicry in Plants. [[Scientific American]] '''257'''(3): 76-83. Among the [[plant pathogen]]s that affect this genus are the [[sac fungus]] ''[[Cochliobolus sativus]]'', which has been noted on common barnyard grass, and [[rice hoja blanca virus]]. Both affect many other grass species, in particular most important cereals, and ''Echinochloa'' weeds may serve as a [[Natural reservoir|reservoir]]. The fungi ''[[Drechslera monoceras]]'' and ''[[Exserohilum monoceras]]'' have been evaluated with some success as potential [[biological pest control|biocontrol]] agents of common barnyard grass in rice fields. More research is necessary, however, because they may not be [[Host (biology)|host-specific]] enough to be of practical use.{{aut|Huang, S.W.; Watson, A.K.; Duan, G.F. & Yu, L.Q.}} (2001): Preliminary evaluation of potential pathogenic fungi as bioherbicides of barnyardgrass (''Echinochloa crus-galli'') in China. International Rice Research Institute Notes '''26'''(2): 36-37. [http://www.irri.org/publications/irrn/pdfs/vol26no2/irrn262pestsci.pdf PDF fulltext] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100705073019/http://www.irri.org/publications/irrn/pdfs/vol26no2/irrn262pestsci.pdf |date=2010-07-05 }} Insect pests include ''[[Atherigona falcata]]'', the barnyard millet shoot fly.{{cite book|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/book/9780128042434/insect-pests-of-millets|title=Insect Pests of Millets: Systematics, Bionomics, and Management|year=2017|first1=A.|last1=Kalaisekar|first2=P.G.|last2=Padmaja|first3=V.R.|last3=Bhagwat|first4=J.V.|last4=Patil|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-804243-4}} ==Species== ; Species[http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/search?q=Echinochloa The Plant List search for Echinochloa][http://bonap.net/NAPA/TaxonMaps/Genus/County/Echinochloa Biota of North America Program 2013 county distribution maps]Gould, F.
